facts.text: His name is Jayden Jackson and he is 45 years old.
He was recently diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); his health history is otherwise unremarkable.
His father has a history of heart disease and stroke.
He is on Medrol (methylprednisolone) for one more week and Plaquenil (hydroxychloroquine).
He gets pain and a feeling of fullness (4/10) in the small joints of both hands in the mornings, lasting 30-60 minutes.
He works full-time as an independent insurance agent at a local insurance company, enjoys meeting new people, and is proud of recently being named top agent in his region.
He lives in a duplex with his wife and two small children.

He is a supportive husband and involved father - a son and a daughter - and loves being a positive role model. They enjoy family nights and recently started a common garden with their duplex neighbors.

He volunteers as a group leader for junior-high boys at the local middle school, leading an after-school running program where the boys work toward running one or more cumulative marathons a semester.
He plays pick-up basketball with friends at the YMCA and lifts weights a few times a week. He also enjoys running, playing with his kids, and gardening.
He is active 6 days a week, 60-120 minutes a day, with muscle-strengthening 3 times a week at moderate intensity. He is inactive about 6-8 hours a day (desk work).

He is concerned about not being able to continue his lifestyle with his new condition. He wants to stay active with his kids, friends, and weights - 'all of the above for as long as I can' - and is seeking advice on wellness with a chronic condition.

His PROMIS emotional screen was unremarkable: Anxiety 50, Depression 50, Fatigue 55, Sleep Disturbance 50; PROMIS Global Health 55. No cognitive or mental-health concerns flagged. His self-efficacy is high and his family is very supportive.
He sleeps 7-8 hours, feels rested, and rates his sleep good - occasionally disturbed by the kids. His condition is not affecting his sleep; no insomnia, snoring, or apnea signs.
He eats about 3 servings of fruits/vegetables and 4 servings of processed food a day and drinks about 80 oz of water. His 'Starting The Conversation' nutrition screen score was 8.
He is a nonsmoker. He has drinks containing alcohol about 4 times per week, 1-2 standard drinks on a typical day, and never six or more on one occasion.

At his annual PT visit: resting heart rate 60, blood pressure 120/78, respiratory rate 12, oxygen 98%. BMI 25, waist 32 inches. Vision 20/20, no hearing loss, skin clear, sensation intact, posture normal.

Performance testing: 1-mile run in 7 minutes, Hexagon Agility Test 18 s, Four-Square Step Test 12 s, 10-meter walk at 1.5 m/s, five-times sit-to-stand 8 s, push-up test 30 s, grip strength 50 kg left / 55 kg right, Apley scratch fingers overlap comfortably, sit-and-reach 35 cm. No movement-screen impairments.
He is insured, a college graduate, with enough food and adequate housing.

His PAVING wellness wheel totals: Stress 16, Attitude 22, Time-outs 18, Variety 15, Energy 20, Nutrition 19, Sleep 20, Investigations 11, Purpose 22, Social 21 (Physical Activity and Goals totals not legible in the source document).
